evidence.why: Shows construction, allocation-error path, request-result assignment, and cleanup.
Shows retry and polling conditions, ACK validation, and failure return without an accepted reply.

facts.rationale: Corrects the implication that completion requires successful acknowledgement. The allocation guard permits an immediate error return, and the request helper can finish without an accepted reply and return kWaitACKError.
facts.value: Constructs a MetroTRK stopped-target or exception notification and attempts synchronous delivery to the development host through an acknowledged request exchange. Returns an allocation error if no outbound buffer is obtained; otherwise returns the request result after cleanup, including failure when no acceptable acknowledgement is obtained.
